rounds.plan: Advance straight down the open central corridor, watching for a mirror wall blocking it
Wall ahead; turn right toward the green-tinted beacon on the right, then step forward and reassess

Surrounded by mirrors on three headings so far; rotate right once more and probe that corridor
Probe blocked ahead; perform a full 6-way rotation scan to find the real green beacon direction before committing
Scan complete; current heading was previously movable, so push forward into the corridor and reassess

Probe the neighboring heading for an opening
Open aisle appears to continue straight ahead; advance along it
Mirror directly ahead. Rotate right without moving to inspect the new reflection geometry
Aisle appears open ahead after the turn; advance to explore
Mirror image of the robot directly ahead confirms a mirror wall, not open floor. Turn right and test that heading
Facing a mirror wall. Sweep clockwise with probe steps to find the actual open direction without burning a decision per heading
Ahead the corridor looks clear between the mirror panels; advance two cells and re-check for green
Blind right-leaning wall-follow: turn right, push forward in bursts, turning right again after each burst to trace around mirror panels

Exhaustive 6-heading probe from this cell: alternate right-turn and forward attempt to identify which adjacent cells are actually open
Stop probing cell-by-cell. Execute a long right-drifting sweep (five forward bursts then a right turn, six times) to cover ground and get out of this mirror pocket
Gather full 360° coverage in one decision: rotate right five times to capture all six headings, then choose the genuinely open neighbor
Corridor ahead looks open (no near-field mirror band); advance along heading 4 to a new cell and reassess
Escape this mirror pocket by wall-following: alternate left turns with three-forward bursts, then try right turns if left stays blocked
Switch to disciplined left-hand wall-following: try turning left and stepping; I'll adapt based on the outcome each round
Scan all six headings from this cell in one decision so the next move is informed rather than guessed
Heading A is a mirror wall (my own reflection fills the frame); the one-right view looked the most open, so rotate right back to it and step forward
One full 6-heading probe cycle (forward attempt + right turn each step) to finally pinpoint the single open exit from this pocket
The last two probes showed I turned off a corridor; rotate back to continue along the corridor I came down and advance two cells
Break out of this reflective pocket with a long biased-walk sweep: advance, wobble right, advance, wobble left, repeated many times to cover ground
Escape the mirror pocket with a repeated probe-and-rotate sweep (forward attempt then right turn, many cycles) so every open heading is found regardless of reflections
This heading shows the open-corridor view (floor tiles and rings receding, no close mirrored self); advance, then turn right to catch the next corridor
Post-turn view shows open floor with nearby decals and no close mirrored self; probe one step forward to test, stopping if it hits
My own reflection fills the frame, so ahead is a mirror. Sweep right with probe steps until a move succeeds
Mirror ahead confirmed by near-field self-reflection. Continue the right-hand probe cycle (turn right, try forward) repeatedly to ride the open spiral corridor out of this pocket
Full 360° rotation scan (6 right turns) to capture every heading from this cell, so I can pick the direction with the most distant self-reflection (= open corridor) before moving
Comparing the six headings, the H+2 view showed the self-reflection smallest/farthest = longest open sight line. Rotate back two steps to that heading and advance
All views here show a close self-reflection (mirror). Capture a full 360° rotation (5 right turns) in one decision to find the heading with the most distant/absent self-reflection = the open corridor
The view at heading h3 (small distant reflection = longest open sight line) is the only one without a close self-reflection. Rotate right four times back to it and advance down that corridor

Stop over-analyzing reflections. Run a long, cheap zigzag wander (4-cell bursts alternating right/left turns, repeated many times) to cover ground across the maze; decision cost is 1 while collisions are only a secondary penalty
Long-standing pocket; run repeated two-forward-plus-right-turn cycles to drift along whichever heading is actually open and break out
Stop zig-zagging after every step — corridors here run straight. Push straight ahead repeatedly in one batch (only the first steps may move if a mirror blocks)
Mirror confirmed dead ahead. Sweep the remaining five headings in one decision so I can choose a genuinely open direction

Rotating and probing one heading per decision is wasting decisions. Execute many full 6-heading probe cycles in a single decision (forward attempt + right turn, repeated), guaranteeing at least one cell of progress per cycle and maximal coverage
Facing a fresh heading; push a long straight run to cover ground in this plaza, then reassess before turning

Use a large self-correcting probe sweep: repeat (forward attempt, then right turn) many times. Every 6-pair cycle tries all six headings, so at least one move is guaranteed per cycle while the heading offset lets it work around mirrors; the run stops automatically on reaching the beacon.
